2.0.0.en: "Ephesus": the capital of the province of Asia Minor at that time. Its church was founded by St. Paul and then became a center for the ministry of St. John as well. It was famous because it was a seaport and because of the famous pagan temple of "Artemis" there, and it was known for its corruption and at first for its resistance to Christianity. It gradually lost its fame after the center of Christianity moved to Constantinople in the fourth century, and it was completely destroyed by the Turks in the fourteenth century.

2.0.1.en: "The angel of the church": there is no certainty about the person of the bishop of this church, but he is one of two persons and no third: either St. Timothy, the disciple of the Apostle Paul, or the bishop "Onesimus" mentioned in the letters of St. Ignatius.

2.0.2.en: "He that holdeth... who walketh": see the explanation of (ch. 1:13-16); the reference here is to the authority and care of the Lord Christ for the bishops and the churches.

2.1.0.en: I know thy works and thy labour: the Lord Christ begins by presenting Himself with the attribute of "the One who knows," that is, the One who searches and knows everything, an attribute we must always remember... for remembering it reminds us of the just judgment if we neglect, and gives us hope that every labor and struggle offered for God's sake is not forgotten before Him. Thy patience: a testimony from Christ to the striving, patience and endurance of His servant.

2.1.1.en: Thou canst not bear: another praise from the Lord Christ to this bishop, that his soul cannot bear to be reconciled with the wicked, or to go along with them or agree with them in their evil.

2.1.2.en: Hast tried: that is, you examined their claim, their preaching and their false pretensions that they were Christians, and found them to be infiltrating Jews whose whole aim was to destroy the Christian faith.

2.1.3.en: He praises the angel of the church for his service and his labors in it, his patient endurance of tribulations, his rejection of the words of the wicked and his care in examining the false teachers in order to expose their false teachings.

2.2.0.en: He continues praising the bishop in the previous verse, and adds a new attribute, that he "hast not fainted."

2.2.1.en: This is the attribute of perseverance in service, which does not know or acknowledge frustration and despair.

2.2.2.en: This bishop was distinguished by labor in service and patience in tribulations. May you not grumble at the abundance of responsibilities or at others troubling you, for your labor is very precious to God and He will reward you for it, so persevere in it for His sake.

2.3.0.en: After the Lord Christ praised His bishop for the virtues he enjoyed in his pastoral life, He begins to direct a rebuke to him, and may we learn this quality from the Lord Christ, which He used with all the bishops, because it carries much gentleness and sensitivity toward the other, and it is praise before reproof. I have somewhat against thee: that is, there is something held against you and for which you are condemned.

2.3.1.en: Thou hast left thy first love: this is the sickness of this church or of its bishop; with the abundance of work, service, problems and wars, the feelings of his first love for Christ were lost, and lukewarmness and routine entered the spiritual life, a sickness that a person may not feel but which before God is a great evil, for "if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned" (Song 8:7).

2.4.0.en: The Lord Christ goes straight into the remedy....

2.4.1.en: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent: return to yourself and examine it, and search for the causes of the beginning of this fall in your love toward Me, and when you grasp these causes you can offer a true repentance in order to avoid what made you fall into this sickness... and the Lord Christ teaches us in the parable of the prodigal son that repentance and return began with an examination of the soul, "he came to himself" (Lk 15:17), which the Church also makes us aware of and teaches us.

2.4.2.en: Take care to set aside a few minutes in which you sit with God and your soul before meeting your father of confession, so that your repentance may be sound.

2.4.3.en: And do the first works: return to what you used to do before with love, and perhaps what is meant here is the works of the inner chamber, such as fervent prayer that kindles the heart with the love of God.

2.4.4.en: I will come unto thee quickly...: the second coming is not what is meant, but rather a warning of an earthly punishment for the one who does not repent or does not respond to the warning, for God, in His love and tenderness toward His creation, is also just and corrects those who do not repent, and so He sometimes allows them an earthly punishment if this benefits them. And remove thy candlestick: that is, your position as a bishop or servant, since you ought to have been a light to your people. The lampstand also comes to mean the Church, and if the Church does not repent of its sin, such as its concern for administrative matters at the expense of spiritual matters and the love of God, its destiny too will be to vanish.

2.4.5.en: He gives him a solution to his problem, which is quick repentance and a return to his first worship and services with care and fervor, and He warns him that if he does not repent He will punish him and he will lose his standing with God, and his service may be taken from him.

2.5.0.en: After the Lord Christ's severe blame and His presentation of the decisive remedy for this church and its bishop, He returns to encourage before He concludes His words....

2.5.1.en: But this thou hast: that is, it is counted to your credit... and it is the opposite of the expression "I have somewhat against thee."

2.5.2.en: The deeds of the Nicolaitans: they are the followers of "Nicolas," one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5), and it was attributed to them that they permitted "fornication..."!! and gluttony in pleasures without restraint, and for this reason the Church excommunicated them, but they found a place in "Ephesus," and for this reason the bishop resisted and rebuked them.

2.5.3.en: Here He returned and encouraged him for his exactness in the faith and his rejection of the heretics, who are the Nicolaitans.

2.5.4.en: Christ rejoices when He finds His servant hating what He does not love... and this statement is for all of us; therefore, my God, we ask Your Holy Spirit to work in us with power so that our will may be united with Your will, and we do not do or make anything contrary to Your pleasure or without Your will.

2.6.0.en: He that hath an ear, let him hear: an expression the Lord used with the churches, and its meaning is that one must hear the voice and act upon it, and that whoever ignores the word of God is like the deaf man who has no ears.

2.6.1.en: What the Spirit saith: that is, what the Lord Christ declared in His vision to John, the Holy Spirit also declares to the churches in every time and place, and these declarations, as we said before, must be obeyed and carried out. To him that overcometh: an expression that is also repeated, and it is rich in its meanings:

2.6.2.en: (1) That is, the possibility of victory and overcoming is available to all believers and is not difficult as long as they love and obey God.

2.6.3.en: (2) That defeat goes back to the person himself if he rejects the commandment and the work of the Holy Spirit in his life. (3) That there are some who may lose everything, whatever their standing in the Church; salvation is not guaranteed to a person as long as he does not safeguard it by constant repentance and spiritual striving, even if he is a bishop. The tree of life: points to Christ Himself, as the most precious reward for the one who overcomes, who enjoys being satisfied with Him in Paradise and eternal life, and the phrase "in the midst of the paradise" points to the presence of Christ in the midst of all His children, and that the sight of Him will be available to all.

2.6.4.en: He calls him to obey these words addressed to him and encourages him with the reward he will receive, which is to be satisfied with Christ in eternity.

2.7.0.en: Smyrna: a city lying north of Ephesus, a port on the Aegean Sea, famous for trade and wealth; today it is known by the name of the Turkish city (Izmir)... Its bishop was the martyr "Polycarp," the disciple of St. John the Apostle, and the church of Smyrna is the only church that the Lord Christ did not rebuke for a clear fault like the rest of the churches, but His letter to it was rather a letter of encouragement.

2.7.1.en: The first and the last... was dead, and is alive: see the explanation of ch. 1:11, 17, 18.

2.7.2.en: Since the church of Smyrna was a church suffering from persecution and torments unto death, the Lord here presents Himself as the eternal, everlasting God so that it may make light of the temporary sufferings, because its God lifts it above temporal sufferings and gives it eternal life; and He is also a conqueror who passed through death and defeated it by the Resurrection, to give the Church comfort that He suffered before as it suffers now, so He shares with it and it imitates Him; likewise He gives it hope that after death there is life and after persecution eternal happiness.

2.8.0.en: I know thy works, and tribulation: a word of encouragement for the bishop and the church: all your labor and endurance are before Me, and I never forget the labor of love or the endurance of tribulations for My name's sake.

2.8.1.en: And poverty: that is, your material poverty in the midst of the rich city of Smyrna, and it is one of the tribulations through which the church passed.

2.8.2.en: But thou art rich: but what the world sees in you as poverty I see as riches, for you are rich in your sound faith and your example to your church.

2.8.3.en: The blasphemy of them which say they are...: here the Lord makes clear to us that the first thorn of persecution was from the Jews who resisted Christianity violently, believing by that that they were true Jews pleasing God, but Christ describes everyone who persecutes His Church as a synagogue of Satan.

2.8.4.en: My dear friend... which is more important to you... to be rich in the sight of God or in the world by its material measures? May we be poor in the world but rich toward God... for just as material wealth has many wars, so spiritual wealth has many blessings; only then do we understand the saying of the Apostle Paul, "as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things" (2 Cor 6:10). So care for your spiritual life and do not be troubled by financial tribulations, however much those around you grow rich.

2.9.0.en: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: the Lord Christ increases His encouragement of the Church and His support of it, and affirms that the suffering will continue for another period, and He also reveals to us that Satan, in his envy and fury, is the one who plans the persecution of the new Church so that its faith may perish; but the Church must not fear as long as Christ supports it in its sufferings, even if Satan in his first rounds is able to cast some of them into prison.

2.9.1.en: Ten days: the expression here is symbolic and does not indicate its literal meaning but expresses shortness; what is meant is that, despite the severity of the tribulation, it will be limited in duration, especially when compared with the unlimited glories of eternity.

2.9.2.en: The Lord Christ increases His encouragement of the bishop of this church by urging him: Be thou faithful, to stand firm in the faith to the end of life, for the reward is great in return when God crowns him with the crown of happiness in eternal life. That God may remove the harshness of the trial from him, He let him know that it is temporary and encouraged him to continue holding fast to his faith and his faithfulness in his life, because He has prepared for him a great crown in heaven.

2.10.0.en: The second death: the first death is the death of the body, which all men will pass through, but the second death is spiritual death and eternal perdition, a death that does not touch the believers who obtain the crown of life; and this is what the Lord said of it, "If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death" (Jn 8:51). St. John will explain more about this subject in the twentieth chapter when he speaks of the millennial kingdom.

2.10.1.en: Much suffering and persecution wears on the souls of many, so that they leave the way... but relying on the divine promises and remembering them casts out fear and frustration and renews the spirit of perseverance, striving and endurance... so grant us, our God, to pass through the second death to the crown of life, not disturbed by the lightness of temporary tribulations, for they are a cause of blessing and work for us a weight of eternal glory...

2.11.0.en: The bishop of the church here is the martyr Carpus, as the historian Eusebius mentioned. Pergamos: it lay on a high mountain and was famous for its library, its abundant cultures and its philosophical schools. He which hath the sharp sword with two edges: since this church was known for lack of exactness and for being influenced by many of the ideas around it, the Lord Christ presented Himself here in the image of the decisive judge, whose word is conclusive and divides between what is true in the faith and what is false (see ch. 1:16, and see also the explanation of v. 16).

2.12.0.en: Where thou dwellest... where Satan's seat is: the Lord Christ affirms, as He affirmed to all the churches, that He knows the conditions and circumstances of every church, and Pergamos in particular was famous for its pagan worship, since it had many pagan temples, such as the temple of Zeus, the temple of Minerva, the temple of Apollo, and the worship of Asclepius, the god of medicine, and for this reason it deserved the title seat of Satan.

2.12.1.en: Thou holdest fast my name: praise of the bishop of Pergamos, who, despite the strength of the opposing current, did not deny his faith even in the worst days of persecution, which reached martyrdom, as happened with "Antipas," who died burned, refusing compromises, so that he deserved to be called by the Lord "my faithful martyr..."

2.12.2.en: Notice, beloved, that all we know about "Antipas," this faithful martyr, is only a few lines written by the historian Andreas; but God does not forget anyone's labor, and He praises this martyr and mentions him in His holy book... so do not care to be known among men, but to be praised by God, who sees in secret and rewards openly.

2.13.0.en: I have a few things against thee: a gentle rebuke that is not without firmness, and it is also considered an introduction to diagnosing the sickness of the church.

2.13.1.en: The doctrine of Balaam: Balaam was a prophet who lived among the Gentiles, and when the kings of the Gentiles feared the people of the children of Israel coming from the wilderness of Sinai to take their lands, they hired Balaam to curse them, but God prevented him from doing so. And before the offers of money presented by "Balak," king of Moab, Balaam weakened, and he did not curse the people of God, but at the same time he deceived God, for he told "Balak" that if this people sinned by fornication their God would be angry with them and leave them, and this is what "Balak" actually did by presenting the Moabite women as a stumblingblock to the people of Israel, and they committed fornication with them and Balak triumphed over them (see the Book of Numbers, chs. 22-25)... The meaning intended here is that in the church of "Pergamos" there were people who incited the believing Christians to take part in the feasts of what was sacrificed to idols, which would be the beginning of the stumblingblock and God's wrath upon them.

2.13.2.en: The teaching here is for all of us, so we must avoid all the stumblingblocks with which Satan bargains with us, lest he separate us from God.

2.14.0.en: Likewise, in the church of Pergamos there were other people who held the teachings of Nicolas, which were discussed before in (v. 6).

2.15.0.en: Repent: always returning, and the beginning is by repentance, and He mentioned the quick coming as a kind of warning as He did with the church of Ephesus (v. 5). I will fight against them with the sword of my mouth: that is, I will resist them and destroy them by the power of My word, for I will raise up faithful servants and preachers and put My word in their mouths, and no one will be able to stand before them...

2.16.0.en: He that hath an ear, let him hear: see the explanation of (v. 7). To him that overcometh... the hidden manna: victory and overcoming are always the condition for the reward, and the reward here is "the hidden manna."

2.16.1.en: The manna: it is the food that God gave to His people in the wilderness to sustain them (Ex 16...); in the New Testament it is the living Body of Christ which we receive in the Eucharist, and whoever eats it lives forever (Jn 6:33, 50, 51). In eternity the meaning is the constant fellowship with Christ, since Christ becomes our only food. A white stone: this is the second reward after "the manna," and the color white is a metaphor for purity and cleanness, while the expression white stone has a historical background... for it was the custom in the Greek and Roman courts that a white stone was given to acquit the accused and a black stone when he was condemned, and the name of the accused was engraved on the white stone, and he carried it with him always as proof of his innocence...; so also the Lord gives everyone who overcomes a declaration of his righteousness and of his victory that all can see.

2.16.2.en: A new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it: the talk in the Book of Revelation about heaven is tied to everything that is new: "the new Jerusalem" (ch. 3:12), "my new name" (ch. 3:12), the new song (ch. 5:9), the new heaven (ch. 21:1), and all things new (ch. 21:5). The new name here means... the particularity of the relationship between each person who strove and overcame and the Lord Christ, as when a father gives his son a pet name that is not given to any other of his children.

2.16.3.en: Whoever hears and obeys the word of God, He will give him constant satisfaction in heaven, a pure life, a personal relationship with Him and an inexpressible enjoyment.

2.16.4.en: My beloved brother, the Lord's encouragement of us and His gifts are beyond all description, for the delight of His heart is in the gifts of His inheritance which He prepared for us beforehand... so do not let any negligence, laziness, preoccupation, slackness or lack of exactness rob you of what your Christ has prepared for you.

2.17.0.en: The angel of the church: he is the bishop St. "Irenaeus," the disciple of St. Polycarp, who was famous for fervor of spirit.

2.17.1.en: Thyatira: a city lying between Pergamos and Sardis, famous for the worship of "Apollo," the sun god, and for the trade in purple, and it is the town of "Lydia," the seller of purple, and it was said that the sin of this church was flattery at the expense of the truth.

2.17.2.en: The Son of God: a strong declaration by Christ of His divinity, after He used in His Incarnation the expression Son of man to indicate His humanity.

2.17.3.en: Eyes like unto a flame of fire: Christ here presents Himself in a way that suits the state of the church, as we will see later, but the attribute of the eyes here means that He is the One who searches everything, who examines every matter, who exposes crooked sinners, and nothing is hidden from Him.

2.17.4.en: His feet are like fine brass: that is, the purity and clarity of His teaching - the sound faith - and it can also be said, His strength, that is, He is like the brass that crushes His enemies like vessels of pottery.

2.17.5.en: Christ presents Himself to the church of Thyatira, which flatters at the expense of the truth, as the just God who searches everything, and His teachings are the strong truth which shatters all evil.

2.18.0.en: I know... this church and this bishop were distinguished by love, faith, service in the fullness of its giving, endurance, longsuffering and spiritual growth, so the Lord testified to him that the last works are more than the first, but the most important thing that distinguishes him is that he did not lose his first love (v. 4) like the bishop of the church of Ephesus.

2.19.0.en: I have a few things against thee: that is, he also fell into a fault, and the word "a few" perhaps means without intending it.

2.19.1.en: Thou sufferest that woman Jezebel: she is a rich person who entered the church and served in it, and we do not know whether her real name was Jezebel or whether it is a name God gave her because of her likeness to Jezebel the wicked queen, the wife of Ahab king of Israel, whose evil reached its utmost..

2.19.2.en: As for this woman, because of the church's flattery of her for her wealth, she began to claim knowledge - a prophetess - and to teach the simple people to eat things sacrificed to idols, which the Church forbade (Acts 15:29), and to seduce them also to fornication, and the fornication here may be in its spiritual meaning, that is, the distortion of their faith.

2.20.0.en: I gave her space to repent: here the Lord reveals to us His longsuffering with sinners, that perhaps they may use it for their repentance.

2.21.0.en: I will cast her into a bed: that is, I will punish her either with sickness or with what hinders her and paralyzes her movement.

2.21.1.en: Them that commit adultery with her: that is, her disciples and followers and those who flatter her and agree with her, will have a punishment too, and Christ describes the punishment as being a tribulation great in its severity.

2.22.0.en: Death and eternal perdition will be the destiny of everyone who went along with her, and My punishment will be an example to the rest of the churches, which will know and be sure that I am the just God who searches the depths of the soul, and that although I delay with sinners, My punishment is just and I reward every person according to his works.

2.23.0.en: Because God is just in His judgments, He does not take anyone for another's fault, and for this reason He separates between the one who followed evil and deserved punishment and the one who kept himself away from strange teachings, so that God does not bring upon him anything of this.

2.23.1.en: The depths of Satan: an expression meaning experiencing evil to its very end.

2.23.2.en: Other burden: that is, I do not demand of them anything beyond their ability.

2.24.0.en: As for the teaching and sound faith that you have, hold it fast with strength and avoid the deviant ideas of faith until the last days and the end of creation by My coming, because everyone who strives and overcomes by his steadfastness in the faith and by keeping My commandments and doing them, I will give him of My power and My authority; for just as I possess everything, I give My children also a spiritual kingship over the souls of those who are far off (the Gentiles), that is, they can influence them and draw them to the faith.

2.25.0.en: By this authority they shepherd them with spiritual care and lead them (those far from the faith) into the fold of the faith.

2.25.1.en: A rod of iron: a symbol of strength, authority and firmness in leadership and guidance.

2.25.2.en: As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: another image which, like the previous one, shows the strength of the authority of the children of God over the Gentiles or those who are far off, and to indicate also the strength of this given authority the Lord Christ adds another comparison, that just as the authority of the Son (Christ) was complete.. so will be the authority of those of His children who overcome.

2.26.0.en: The morning star: the Lord Christ declared at the end of the Book of Revelation that He Himself is "the bright and morning star" (ch. 22:16), that is, the most precious reward for the one who overcomes is to enjoy the possession of Christ Himself, that is, in eternity He gives Himself to each one of the heirs of His Kingdom.

2.27.1.en: How wonderful is Your giving, Lord, and how wonderful is the beauty of eternity.. how can this be? How can we eat You, O tree of life, and how can we partake of You, O hidden manna, and how can we possess You, O morning star, unlimited in Your glory?! What John wrote is higher than the imagination of any human mind, but we trust in Your word and Your promises, so give us the spirit of striving that we may overcome and enjoy all that You have prepared for us, O Beloved of our souls.. my holy God.

2.27.2.en: Letters to the rest of the seven churches
